# Roadmap

Work top-to-bottom; `/dev-cycle` picks the first unchecked item. Check items off as they land (with tests). Keep milestones honest — an item isn't done until it works in the running app **and** over the control protocol.

## M0 — Foundation ✅
- [x] Repo scaffold, docs, agent fleet, skills
- [x] SPM monorepo: DAWCore / DAWEngine / DAWControl / AIServices / DAWApp
- [x] Domain model v0 (project, tracks, clips, transport, mixer state)
- [x] Control WebSocket server skeleton + command router
- [x] MCP server skeleton with core tool surface
- [x] App shell: dark theme, transport bar, glowing meter component

## M1 — Core audio engine ✅
- [x] Audio file import (wav/aiff/mp3/m4a) onto tracks
- [x] Sample-accurate multitrack playback via engine graph
- [x] Transport: play/stop/seek/loop region, position broadcast to UI + control clients
- [x] Per-track and master metering (peak/RMS) driving the glow meters
- [x] Master volume, per-track volume/pan/mute/solo wired to engine
- [x] Offline render (mixdown to wav) — `render.mixdown` command
- [x] Engine test harness: offline-render assertions (null test, gain test) — determinism null (exact 0.0) + unity-vs-source + gain suite; golden-master null noted as future addition

## M2 — Recording & project persistence
- [x] Record from default input onto armed tracks (`track.setArm`, `transport.record`, host-time-aligned takes) — no round-trip latency compensation yet (M4 PDC)
- [x] Input device enumeration/selection (`input.listDevices`, `input.setDevice`) — pinned-device capture fixed 2026-07-05 (benign config-change triage + first-buffer watchdog; live E2E green for default-uid pin, ZoomAudioDevice pin, and unpinned)
- [x] Punch in/out windows (`transport.setPunch`, writer accept-window)
- [x] Metronome/click with count-in
- [x] `.dawproj` bundle format: versioned JSON + media dir; open/save/autosave
- [x] Undo/redo across all commands (coalescing snapshot journal in DAWCore; `edit.undo`/`edit.redo`, Edit-menu ⌘Z/⇧⌘Z)

## M14 — Gapless loop wrap (seeded 2026-07-12 from the m13-f design spike: docs/research/design-m13f-gapless-loop.md, GO-WITH-CONDITIONS; implementation follows that doc's §9 phases L-1…L-4 and §10 conditions C1–C8 verbatim — deviations return to the design doc for amendment)

**Standing law (C1)**: `GaplessLoopSpikeTests` (the L-0 splice-primitive pins, 4 tests) stays green forever; any splice regression blocks M14 work that day and converts the milestone to NO-GO/park with the spike retained as evidence (m10-p precedent). **Standing law (C4)**: zero new RT surface beyond the bounded cursor re-seek — no allocation, locks, or ObjC on the render path in ANY phase; any deviation returns to the design doc for amendment. Offline/render parity (§7): nothing changes offline, ever — provably (C8).

Caught by the agent reading §6 more carefully than I had; verified firsthand with a standalone `edgecheck.swift` before accepting it.** The fix makes mixer→outputNode EXPLICIT at 48 k, and the topology read-back (`mixer out 48000 / outputNode in 48000 / outputNode out 44100`) is a PER-RUN PRECONDITION THAT FAILS THE RUN — a discarded `connect()` would silently reproduce the old graph and print a clean-looking result from a manipulation that never happened; confirmed on all 46 explicit-arm runs. **THAT MOVE IS ALSO THE CYCLE'S REAL MEASUREMENT: Δ(explicit − implicit) = `+0.948 / +0.935 ms`, so essentially the ENTIRE −0.94 ms belongs to the MIXER's SRC, not the output edge's.** **⚠️ AND THAT −0.94 ms IS NOT A COST ANYTHING PAYS TODAY — I MIS-STATED THIS TO THE USER AND IN THE CHANGELOG AS "the mixer, where it happens today"; CORRECTED 2026-07-31. Production converts NOWHERE: `AudioEngine.init`/`rebuildEngine` pass `graphRate: currentDeviceRate(of: engine)` (AudioEngine.swift:443/:980), so the live graph ADOPTS the device rate and no SRC exists in the steady state (exactly as m19-k's own record already said). The −0.94 ms is the price of building m20-d the NAIVE way — inject the project rate but leave mixer→outputNode implicit — so this probe is a BUILD INSTRUCTION for m20-d, not a defect report against the shipping app. m20-b found no bug; there is nothing here awaiting a fix.** **NUMBERS (N=5/leg, primary shape unless noted).** **P1** (48 k edge over 44.1 k device): 5/5, peak `996.991 Hz`, worst error `0.009 Hz` vs ±1 Hz — resample-by-relabeling would have read 1085.2 Hz. **⚠️ ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION, CAUGHT IN REVIEW AFTER THE FIRST TICK: the topology fix above was applied to `runAnchored` (P2X/P2X-A/P3X) but NOT to `runOnce`, so the P1 figure directly above was measured on `.implicitMixerSRC` — the very shape this record calls a trap four sentences earlier. The pitch-correctness CLAIM was never unsupported: P4's 44.1 k baseline segment is an explicit 48 k output edge over a 44.1 k device and reads the same `996.991 Hz`, and THAT is the output-edge correctness evidence. But the record had pinned the headline correctness leg to the wrong shape. GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same defect wearing a different hat: WHEN YOU FIX A TOPOLOGY/CONFIG BUG, ENUMERATE EVERY CALL SITE THAT BUILDS THAT THING — fixing the two legs whose numbers looked wrong left the leg whose number looked RIGHT still on the broken shape, and a correct-looking number is exactly what stops you re-checking. `runOnce` has since been given the same no-default `Topology` parameter and P1/P1-F re-run on `.explicitOutputEdge`; see the re-run line at the end of this record. **P2X** (explicit output edge + passthrough): constant `+0.025 ms`, spread `0.022 ms` vs one device quantum `11.610 ms` (512 frames); `lastRenderTime.sampleTime` mean slope `44101.0 Hz` — **1.0 Hz from the device rate, 3899.0 Hz from the project rate**, so the output edge is unambiguously in the DEVICE clock domain (B1/B2 paired). **P2X-A** (explicit, no effect): PASS, spread `0.012 ms`. **P3X**: `+0.004 ms` added latency. **P4** (44.1→48→96 k mid-play, restart WITHOUT reconnect): 10/10 flips, 15/15 rate points, worst pitch error `0.020 Hz`; edge input scope read 48 k before AND after every restart; `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` arrived 10/10. All of 44.1/48/96 k are supported (`AvailableNominalSampleRates` = 8k…768k), so the skip path never fired. **P5 — NOT RUN**: BlackHole 2ch is stereo-only and staging a mono/aggregate device would mean creating a system audio device; §6 marks P5 opportunistic and explicitly not gateable, so this is a recorded non-result, not a gap. **EVERY LEG HAS A FALSIFIABILITY SIBLING, because five byte-identical runs look the same as a probe printing a constant.** P1-F: same path at 440 Hz reads `439.993 Hz`. P3-F/P3X-F: a known 10.000 ms of injected leading silence is observed as `+10.004`/`+9.995 ms`. P4's capture-side control inverts into a proof — a capture asked for a 44.1 k client format over a 96 k device BUILDS AND STARTS CLEANLY and then delivers ZERO frames, so a flip that had not really taken would have starved the capture and produced a NIL pitch, never a wrong one. **A HYPOTHESIS OF MINE WAS FALSIFIED BY THE DATA AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE:** I predicted the implicit arm's NEGATIVE latency (`−0.94 ms`) was an artifact of the fixed `abs > 0.05` onset threshold tripping early on the converter's smeared edge, and briefed the agent to treat it that way. An energy-envelope estimator (50 %-of-plateau, ~5× less edge-sensitive) reproduced it to within `0.010 ms` at two window sizes. **It is a real property of the mixer-SRC graph's anchor-to-output mapping, not a detection bias — and the cautionary phrasing does not apply to the output-edge arm at all, whose figure is POSITIVE.** **OTHER FINDINGS WORTH CARRYING:** (a) **SDK, 10/10 flips — after a configuration change `engine.isRunning == false` while `player.isPlaying == true`; any recovery path gating on `player.isPlaying` gets a FALSE POSITIVE** (check against the real `recoverEngine` at Phase 2). (b) **At a 48 k device rate the "edge still reports 48 k" criterion is a CONSTANT FIELD and cannot discriminate** — "persisted" and "silently re-derived to the device rate" print the same number; read P4's 15/15 as **10 discriminating + 5 consistent-but-mute**. (c) The §6 passthrough is `AVAudioUnitEQ(numberOfBands: 0)`, proven unity rather than assumed — an offline null test gave worst `|out − in| = 0.000e+00` over 48000 frames and `latency = 0.0 s`; inserting it changed the constant by `−0.008/+0.010 ms`, i.e. nothing. **ENVIRONMENT HAZARDS, both real and both caught by instrumentation rather than by luck:** BlackHole **WEDGED once** — it accepted `AudioDeviceStart` (rc 0, `IsRunning`→1) and delivered **ZERO IOProc callbacks**, silence indistinguishable from a broken converter; triggered after an UNCATCHABLE ObjC exception (`player did not see an IO cycle`) killed the process mid-stream while it held the device started, which also bypassed the rate restore. Answered by `waitForIOCycle` (prevents the abort), `run.sh` (restores the rate from a signal trap, proven by aborting a stub), and `halcheck` (raw-HAL preflight; healthy ≈172 @44.1k / ≈188 @48k / ≈376 @96k, zero = wedged). Recovery is `sudo killall coreaudiod` — **the user's call, never the probe's.** Second hazard: a pass-1 P4 run failed when **the user's AirPods connected mid-run**, re-enumerating devices so AVAudioEngine's output AUHAL fell back to the new system default (`pinnedDev=197`, a device absent from the list); halcheck read 376 immediately after, so NOT a wedge. **The `pinnedDevice` read-back is exactly what turned that into a legible routing diagnosis instead of a converter fault.** **SAFETY, deliberate deviation from §6:** the design doc says to make BlackHole the DEFAULT OUTPUT; that would silence the user's speakers machine-wide, so both units are pinned at the AUHAL and **the system default was never read-modify-written**. The only device setting written anywhere is BlackHole's nominal rate — §6's named test surface — restored on every exit path (verified back at its 48000 entry rate). `ZoomAudioDevice`/`ParrotAudioPlugin`/built-ins never opened. **Routing note: done by `audio-dsp-engineer` across three delegations**, after the user corrected a standing misreading that had been keeping this work in the main context. **P1 RE-RUN ON `.explicitOutputEdge` (4th delegation, post-review — closes the attribution gap flagged above): `996.991 Hz` 5/5, worst error `0.009 Hz`; P1-F control `439.993 Hz` with the 997 Hz criterion NOT met, as required. BYTE-IDENTICAL to the implicit figures — `frames`/`peak`/`rms` too.** ⚠️ **AND IDENTITY HERE IS THE EXPECTED RESULT, NOT A FINDING, WHICH IS WHY IT MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE: a mixer at unity with a single input is a passthrough, so both topologies hand the SAME converter the SAME 48 k sine; and P1 could not have resolved a difference regardless — the 65536-point FFT at 44100 Hz has a `0.672913 Hz` bin and the 0.009 Hz error is ~1/75 of one. **THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE THE TWO TOPOLOGIES ARE EQUIVALENT** — P2X-A/P3X carry that question and their answer is the opposite (`+0.948 ms`).** What DOES prove the graph actually changed is a positive printed discrimination, pre-registered from the prior log before re-running: the per-run topology read-back triple, which reads `mixerOut=44100 edgeIn=44100 edgeOut=44100` on the implicit arm and `48000/48000/44100` on the explicit one — **verified firsthand across both logs, not taken from the agent's report** (9 implicit / 13 explicit triples in the old log; all 5 new P1 runs explicit). A same-number result with no such discriminator would have been indistinguishable from an edit that never took effect. **THE AGENT THEN FOUND A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE VERY BUG IT WAS SENT TO FIX** — the summary block still grouped P1 under an `IMPLICIT topology` heading, so the next default full-ladder run would have printed a true P1 PASS under a false topology label; fixed, along with two stale comments asserting `runOnce` leaves the output edge implicit. That is the enumerate-every-call-site lesson recurring inside its own repair. **TWO CARRY-FORWARD CAVEATS.** (1) My brief asserted a leg-selection mechanism existed; it did not — `m20b` ignores argv entirely, so `M20B_ONLY_P1` is a NEW knob, not a discovered one (early-exit sited after P1-F; the default unset run is still the full ladder). (2) To avoid a divergent second copy, `connectEdges`/`topologyReadBack` were extracted from `runAnchored` and shared with `runOnce` — **so the published P2/P3/P2X/P3X numbers were taken on the PRE-refactor tree and P2 was NOT re-run against the post-refactor one.** **THE RECORDED CONSTANTS ARE UNAFFECTED, AND THAT — NOT THE PROBE'S DISPOSABILITY — IS WHY NO RE-RUN WAS OWED: they are measurements of code that actually ran, and a refactor applied afterwards cannot retroactively change what a completed measurement read.** The extraction being mechanical, and the probe being scratchpad-only (never shipped; m20-d's gate is the live app, not this probe), is only why it was not worth another device-touching pass for the SEPARATE question of whether the probe still reproduces them. So: the constants above stand as written and are not stale — but a future re-run that disagrees with them should suspect THIS refactor first, not measurement flake.

The agent then measured WHICH action storms: flip alone → 0 in both arms; **parameter-only mutation (`track.setVolume`) → 0 real / 41 mutant, THE STORM**; teardown-class mutation (add+remove track) → 0 in both, because by then the mutant has already re-keyed. **A gate that used only the teardown-class change — the obvious design, and the one m20-d used — would have read ZERO re-prepares in the mutant and gone confidently hollow.** The param-only mutation is the trigger precisely because it is the FIRST `tracksDidChange` after the flip.
  **THE SEAM (no new wire surface):** `note.audition`'s `reason` field. `auditionAudibility` (`AudioEngine.swift:1313`, read firsthand) checks `auRegistry.preparedInstrument(forTrack:) == nil` synchronously and returns `.inaudibleNotReady` — the registry's own prepared state on an existing verb. ⚠️ It is PRIORITY-ORDERED behind mute/solo, `!isRunning` and `noRenderer`, so a single sample can be masked; the legs therefore ask "did `instrumentNotReady` EVER appear in this window", never "what was the reason at time T".

On the real tree that leg is deterministically green — a constant rate cannot move whenever the rebuild lands, which is m20-d's whole point.** Storm COUNTS vary run to run (the hammer samples a millisecond-scale window); what reproduced exactly across both mutant runs is the SET of legs that redden, minus that race.
  **⚠️ THE FINAL-STATE TRAP, worth carrying to any future rate gate: at the END of the run the MUTANT reads 48000 too**, because its last rebuild happened with the device back at 48 kHz. - [x] (m23-a) **Mixer strip layout: the m22-e insert-chip REGRESSION, plus panel collapse + a volume knob.** User report: "in Mix tab when it adds inserts and other instruments or effects it eclipses the volume scales." m22-e is what ADDED insert chips with five-cell activity bars, and the tested bundle contains it — treat as a shipped-quality regression and fix FIRST. Three parts: (1) the strip must reserve the fader/scale region so inserts can never overlap it (`Sources/DAWApp/Mixer/MixerStripView.swift`, 37.7 KB — the layout owner); (2) a collapsible instrument/insert top panel so manual fader work always has room; (3) a round VolumeKnob beside the existing `PanKnob` (`MixerControls.swift:99` is the precedent to mirror — same idiom, no new mechanism). Pure-view work: wire/MCP delta ZERO. Route: ui-design-engineer. GATE: staging captures at both densities with a full insert chain proving no overlap, Simple/Pro flip, suites. — **DONE 2026-07-26 (ui-design-engineer).** Root cause was one line: the fader's hard `.frame(minHeight: 150)`. A hard minimum is exported UP to a console that has no vertical scroll, so a growing chain made the whole mixer demand more height than the window had. **Blast radius was wider than the report:** at 760 pt the app header row AND transport bar were pushed clean off-window before any strip clipped; at 640 the strip clipped BOTH ends (an over-tall `VStack` centres and spills both ways — track name at the top, dB + Mute/Solo/Arm at the bottom). The master strip was a SEPARATE contributor with its own larger minimum; fixing channels alone would have left it. FIX: `MixerStripLayout` (new, headless `DAWAppKit`) splits a strip into a RESERVED cluster that never yields (header · VOL|PAN · fader+meter+dB · Mute/Solo/Arm) and exactly ONE yielding region (the Pro signal-flow block). `signalFlowRoom(available) = max(0, min(available*0.55, available − reserved))` — **content-independent, which is why it holds at any chain length**. The region is a bounded `ScrollView(.vertical).frame(maxHeight: room).fixedSize(vertical: true)`: `fixedSize` is load-bearing (a ScrollView's ideal height is its content's, so the region becomes inflexible at `min(content, room)` and the greedy fader absorbs the rest). Implementer REPLACED its own first cut — `ViewThatFits + maxHeight + layoutPriority(1)` passed the letter of its gate but left a 2-insert strip holding a ~200 pt void with the fader crammed at the bottom (a `maxHeight` frame stretches to whatever it is proposed): **the guard rail was reintroducing the failure it exists to remove.** Collapse disclosure PERSISTS as `panelLayout.mixerInsertsCollapsed` (console-wide, app-sticky, default EXPANDED so chains don't vanish on update; a disclosure, not a density mode → no chip; inventory verdict at simple-pro-inventory.md:216). `VolumeKnob` additive (`VerticalFader` untouched), Canvas contract honoured, new shared `KnobGeometry` is now the ONE knob-path home with `PanKnob` refactored onto it; cyan not neutral (volume HAS a meaning-color: fader fill, dB readout, VOLUME automation lane), unipolar from range-min with a unity detent so it cannot disagree with the fader about 0 dB. Explain 88→**89**. DELIBERATE, DISCLOSED DEVIATION — Simple mode DID change (knob row 38→52 pt + the knob; pan readout moved inline to `PAN L64`, a change driven purely by the Pro budget): **ORCH ACCEPTED** — the brief's "Simple must not change" was protecting against REGRESSION, and Simple's regression behaviour is verifiably unchanged (Pro sections still hide whole, freed space still flows to the fader); one row anatomy beats two forked ones, and the knob belongs in Simple most of all. - [x] (m23-b) **Piano-roll keys read as gray because they ARE gray — make them piano.** Verified root cause: `Theme.swift:15-16` sets `keyBlack = 0x11141C` and `keyWhite = 0x2C3242` — BOTH dark, so the "white" keys render dark slate. The user is right and the fix is small. Retone `keyWhite` to a readable ivory and re-balance the grid lane stripes (`PianoRollView.swift:934`) so the black/white alternation reads at a glance without breaking the dark-glass language or note-block contrast. Route: ui-design-engineer. GATE: capture at both densities, note blocks still legible over both lane tones, DESIGN-LANGUAGE compliance note, suites. — **DONE 2026-07-26 (ui-design-engineer).** The roadmap framed this as a retone; it is really an **INK-INVERSION** item, and the naive one-hex change ships a broken gutter. `keyBlack`/`keyWhite` have ONE call site (`KeyboardSidebar.swift:36`) but FOUR house-chrome elements composite on top of the white rows, all light-on-dark by construction — `hairline` separator, `gridEmphasis` octave marker, `textDim` label, `playback` cyan middle C — measuring **1.02/1.05/2.19/1.07:1** on ivory, i.e. invisible. The labels are not an edge case: they draw at `pitch % 12 == 0` and **C is always a white key**. Continuous costs 65x the scroll traffic and **3.3x the main-actor latency** — 49 ms against a ~33 ms transport tick means the main actor is already behind the cadence it is following (the sampler getting 119 replies vs 100 in the same wall-clock window is the same fact from the other side). **The decisive column is `contentWidthChanges: 0` in BOTH**, which is what answers the delegation's stated worry directly: the marker WOULD re-lay-out scroll content per tick, except every target is clamped to `contentWidth - viewport`, which makes the lanes' `totalBeats` zoom padding (`availableWidth + max(0, hScrollApplyTarget)`) a no-op for follow. - [x] (m23-d) **Note audition: hear the pitch while you drag it.** Standard in every note editor and absent here (no audition/preview path in the piano roll — the `audition` hits in `AudioEngine.swift` are m22-g's reference lane, unrelated). Dragging a note vertically, and clicking a key in the sidebar, should sound the pitch on the track's instrument. Needs an engine seam to trigger a one-shot note outside the sequencer schedule, RT-safe and independent of transport state. Route: design pass by daw-architect on the trigger seam (must not perturb the render graph or the scheduled MIDI path), then audio-dsp-engineer. Triple required if a wire command is added (`note.audition` or similar) so the copilot can audition too. GATE: audible one-shot with transport stopped AND during playback without disturbing scheduled notes, no allocation on the render thread, suites. — **DONE 2026-07-26 (audio-dsp-engineer), built to `docs/research/design-note-audition.md`.** Five layers: a SECOND per-renderer `LiveEventRing` (`auditionRing`, cap 64, main actor = the single producer — made a type property by `@MainActor pushAudition`/`beatAuditionHeartbeat` rather than the doc's raw `.push` at the call site); `AuditionOutcome` + `setAuditionPitches`/`stopAllAudition` on `AudioEngineControlling` with protocol-extension defaults so the ~6 test fakes compile untouched; a `@MainActor AuditionController` in DAWCore (8-voice cap, 500 ms heartbeat, 30 s hold ceiling, last-call-wins one-shot); the wire triple `note.audition`; and the piano-roll drag + gutter press behind a debug-tier defeat switch (`debug.panelLayout {auditionEnabled}`, zero wire growth — the wire verb deliberately ignores it). **Liveness is a WATCHDOG, not a duration cap**: the renderer counts its own `renderedFrames` and cuts audition voices after 3 s without a heartbeat, so a crashed or wedged UI can never leave a note stuck, and no clock is ever read on the render thread. **DEVIATION FOUND AND AMENDED, not coded around (§6.3 → AMENDMENT A1):** the design's safety-release loop was unbounded, so on a dense-schedule quantum it wrote PAST the end of the preallocated merge buffer — reproduced first as `11 events out of an 8-slot buffer` (72 bytes past a 192-byte allocation) on the render thread, then closed with a computed `liveBlockBound` and a one-quantum DEFERRAL (6a does not clear the pitch map until the off is actually written, so the next quantum re-emits it — late, never lost). No capacity changed. Two smaller findings reported rather than built: §11.2's `soloExcluded` reason is unreachable given §7.1's merged `inaudibleMuted`, and §8.2's "reproduce the pitch↔y affine inline" was unnecessary (`PianoRollModel.pitch(forY:)` already exists; m16-a's `@Sendable` Canvas constraint binds the DRAWING closure, not a main-actor gesture handler). A hole the design did not cover was found at review and closed: `record()` now releases any HELD audition, because refusing new ones does nothing about a voice already sounding when the take starts — the heartbeat re-asserts it every 500 ms straight through the take and the capture ring cannot see it, so it would be heard and not recorded. **C18 staging gate 20/20** (`scripts/gates/m23d-note-audition.mjs`, port 17695, killed pidfile-exact): asserts AUDIO off `mixer.masterAnalysis`, never an ok response — transport STOPPED −80.00 dB floor → **−10.58 dB** sounding (+69.4) and back to the floor on release; DURING PLAYBACK the audition adds **+7.82 dB** over the running mix while the scheduled notes never fall below −14.44 dB, and after it releases the bus returns to within **0.98 dB** of the scheduled-only level (an `instrument.reset()`/`requestFlush()` would have collapsed it to −80 — that number IS the §5.3 proof); the debug switch OFF still sounds over the wire. Two gate-fixture defects were found and fixed by measurement, not by loosening a threshold: GM program 0 is a DECAYING patch, so both release legs were reading an envelope rather than the code (moved to the sustaining program 16), and "released" cannot be a single absolute dB — a note-off is followed by a release+reverb tail, so the gate samples twice 3 s apart and asserts the SHAPE (collapse −47.15 dB, then −57.73 → −80.00 = decaying tail, where a stuck voice would sit flat). §16 Q1 answered empirically: the first audition after `track.setInstrument` on a cold app answers `audible:false reason:"instrumentNotReady"` and becomes audible after **~250 ms** — `prepare()` from `setAuditionPitches` is necessary but the hosted instrument's async preparation is the real gate. C15 argued structurally line-by-line AND backstopped empirically: `malloc_zone_statistics` `blocks_in_use` delta **0** across 10 000 audition-carrying quanta, 4 runs (one-off probe, not left in the suite). 51 new tests / 5 new suites; Swift **3453/370** 0-warn (4 of 5 full runs fully green; the 5th hit only the known pre-existing `SoundBankHostingTests` T1 AU-preparation flake, which isolates 7/7 in 0.626 s), npm **212/212**; wire 152→**153** commands, 155→**156** router cases, MCP 155→**156** tools, Copilot catalog 65→**66**; both wire files' diffs are purely additive (`Commands.swift` +70/−0; `server.ts` +73/−1, the single deletion being the pre-existing uncommitted m22-g Opus-5 string). **REBUILD REQUIRED — `dist/DAWPro.app` predates this.** **ORCH VERIFICATION 2026-07-26 — TICK HELD (unticked by the orchestrator; the implementer had ticked it). Suites and wire are clean, but the FEATURE misbehaves audibly, so the box cannot stand.** Reproduced independently: Swift **3453/370** 0-warn fully green (the AU flake did not fire on the orch run), npm **212/212**, wire pins 153/156/66 with `note_audition` the only new MCP tool and the sole `server.ts` deletion the pre-existing m22-g Opus-5 string — additive-only holds. **C13 PASSED and is now measured rather than argued**: rendering the same project with a live audition sounding produced a BIT-IDENTICAL file (`eb006812a9338a36…`, 1156096 bytes both), so a held audition can never reach an export. **The defect: the audition note is released immediately instead of held, and a SECOND note sounds at t≈`durationMs`.** The control that makes it airtight is internal to one session on the built-in polySynth — a SCHEDULED 6-beat note holds FLAT at −14.5 dB for 6 s, while a `durationMs:4000` audition traces −12.9 → −77.7 over 4.1 s, which is the exact shape of that instrument's release envelope (measured separately with a 0.25 s scheduled note: −11.0 → −80 over ~4.5 s). Rises >8 dB occur ONLY at 0.15 s and 4.26 s, and the second tracks `durationMs` exactly (2.27 s for 2000, 4.26 s for 4000). **That >8 dB detector alone could NOT have exonerated the heartbeat** — a re-push of an already-open pitch lands on a voice already in release, so it would re-onset QUIETER than the previous peak and never trip an 8 dB rise; sampling at 150 ms cannot resolve a 500 ms sawtooth either. There are exactly two production callers: `AudioEngine.swift:2986` passes `cause: cause` ✓, and **`OfflineRenderer.swift:353` passes nothing**, silently taking `.relocation` (= do not chase held notes). ⚠️ **The silent caller is probably CORRECT and that is not the point.** `.relocation` for an offline render plausibly matches what live playback from the same beat would sound like, so a bounce that drops a note held across a non-zero `fromBeat` arguably matches playback — ~~but nothing anywhere records that this was decided rather than defaulted~~ — ⚠️ **THAT CLAIM IS FALSE AND I WROTE IT. CORRECTED 2026-08-02 at the m23-bv pick.** The decision IS recorded, in **the very file this entry cites**: `NoteChaseSiteTests.swift:47-49` says *"Site 11 (`OfflineRenderer`) is not in this file: it never names a cause, it takes `scheduleAll`'s `.relocation` default — which is what keeps the offline SHA gates byte-identical."* I read `:115` and `:142` of that file and filed an absence without reading its header. **The lesson is the one this project keeps re-learning in a new costume: I searched for the justification where I expected it (beside the code) and declared it missing, when it was in the test's prose 95 lines above the line I quoted.** ⚠️ **What SURVIVES the correction, and it is not nothing:** (1) the recorded justification is CIRCULAR — "it keeps the offline SHA gates byte-identical" is a reason not to CHANGE the behaviour, not a reason the behaviour is musically right, since the gates encode exactly what the code already does; (2) a comment is not a compiler, so a THIRD caller still inherits `.relocation` silently; and (3) the product question below is genuinely open and unanswered by that comment. ⚠️ **REACHABILITY VERIFIED by the orchestrator 2026-08-02 — a non-zero `fromBeat` is an ORDINARY user/agent action, not a theoretical path.** `fromBeat` is wire-exposed on **four** render verbs: `render.bounce` (`Commands.swift:2945`), `render.stems` (`:3054`), `render.measureLoudness` (`:2865`), and the m6 v-b clip vocal-fix windowed bounce (`:928`), plus `:2834`. **So the concrete question is a product question, and it is worth answering deliberately:** given a pad held from bar 1, does `render.bounce fromBeat: <bar 5>` sound like the song does at bar 5? Playing THROUGH bar 5 from the top, the pad is audible — the schedule is continuous and nothing needs chasing. Bouncing FROM bar 5 under `.relocation` starts a fresh schedule with no chase, so the pad is absent. **That is a divergence between a region bounce and the song it is a region of**, and whichever answer is right, right now nothing records that anyone chose it. Do NOT "fix" the offline behaviour blind — first settle whether a region render should chase, then either remove the default and make every caller state its answer, or keep it and write down why. ⚠️ Confirm the drop empirically before acting: whether a note whose start precedes `fromBeat` and whose end follows it is dropped by `scheduleAll` under `.relocation` is the m23-bp chase question and should be MEASURED on this path, not inferred from the flag's name. ⚠️ Also worth deciding whether the site pins should scan `PlaybackGraph.swift` too — a pin that silently covers one file while the discipline spans two reads as coverage it does not have. ⚠️ **SCOPE CONSTRAINT, MEASURED 2026-08-02: "just remove the default" is NOT a two-line change.** `scheduleAll` has **2 production callers but ~30 TEST callers** across 16 files (`GaplessLoop*`, `IdlePlayerSkip`, `BusRoutingRender`, `AutomationEngine`, `EngineNotice`, `EffectChainRender`, `InsertSpectrumCoverage`, `ExceptionArmor`, `MIDIControllerSchedule`, …), nearly all of which omit `cause`. No m23-u gate leg uses CC64, so the residual is untouched and UNPINNED. Fix shape: latch on `pitch == 64` (`velocity >= 64`), cleared on pedal-up and in `clearLiveVoices()`, added as a disjunct at 6d. GATE: pedal down, note on, note OFF, hold > 8 s on a real `PolySynthInstrument` asserting audio. Route: `daw-architect` → `audio-dsp-engineer`. — **DONE 2026-07-30.** FOUR functional lines, exactly the specified shape: `private var livePedalDown` (render-thread-only), the latch in the `kind >= 2` branch, `|| livePedalDown` at 6d, and the clear in `clearLiveVoices()`. **C11 is intact and that was checked, not assumed:** the latch writes one Bool, touches no pitch map, mints no ID and — the part that matters after m23-ad — EMITS NOTHING, so the `emitBound` arithmetic that is now the only thing between a wrong constant and a render-thread overrun is unchanged. Audition needs no equivalent: `:709` documents that kind ≥ 2 is a producer bug there, so `auditionRing` carries no CC. **THE ITEM'S FIX SHAPE HAD A LIVE TRAP AND THE ROADMAP TEXT CONTAINS IT — "latch on `pitch == 64`" IS WRONG ON ITS OWN.** In that branch `pitch` is a controller number ONLY for kind 2: for `pitchBend` it is the LSB and for `channelPressure` it is the value (`MIDISchedule.swift:21-25`). A bare `pitch == 64` latches the pedal ON for a CENTRED bend (LSB 64, MSB 0x40 ≥ 64 — the single most common message in any bend gesture) and OFF for an aftertouch of 64 (velocity 0), the latter silently restoring this very bug. - [x] (m23-at) **PRODUCTION DEFECT, found by the m23-ab-3 characterization: the AU-prepare timeout is not a deadline, and the condition it exists to catch is exactly the condition that disables it.** `AUHostRegistry.raceAgainstTimeout` races two unstructured tasks — `Task { @MainActor in work() }` against `Task { @MainActor in try? await Task.sleep(for: timeout); gate.resume(.timedOut) }`. **Both hops are `@MainActor`, so the sleeping task must RE-ACQUIRE the main actor to fire.** When the main actor is contended the timeout arrives late by an unbounded amount, so `.seconds(10)` means "10 s of sleep PLUS however long it takes to get back onto a busy main actor". **MEASURED (m23-ab-3, and independently reproduced by the orchestrator): under full-suite load GM prepare takes ~20–24 s — ALWAYS past the 10 s wall — yet passes ~75–80% of the time, and elapsed time does NOT predict the outcome (my 19.6 s run FAILED, my 23.8 s run PASSED).** Which task wins is a scheduling coin flip. Isolated, the same prepare is ~45–49 ms, a ~400× gap; pure CPU starvation (20 saturating processes, N=15) does NOT reproduce it, which rules out generic slowness. **Why this matters beyond the test:** [[daw-pro-au-hosting-wedge]] records a third-party AUv2 (Surge XT) wedging the MAIN ACTOR for minutes — precisely the stall this timeout is meant to bound — and a main-actor timeout cannot fire while the main actor is wedged. So the user-facing guard fails in exactly its design case, and can also fire spuriously when the work would have finished. **Fix direction: the deadline must not be main-actor-bound** — schedule it off the main actor (a detached/global-executor task, or `Task.detached` that resumes the gate without needing `@MainActor` re-entry), so the timeout is a real wall clock. GATE: a test that holds the main actor busy past the timeout and proves the timeout still fires within a bounded margin. Route: `audio-dsp-engineer` (RT/host path) with `daw-architect` review — this touches AU-host lifecycle. **Do NOT just raise the 10 s number; that makes a broken deadline slower, not correct.** **DONE 2026-07-29 (m23-at).** **The diagnosis in this line was right and the fix direction it named was right; the SCOPE it implied was too generous, and the close-out says so.** Shipped: `Sources/DAWCore/DeadlineRace.swift` — a `nonisolated` entry point racing `@MainActor` work against a deadline on a `Task.detached`, with a lock-guarded once-gate (`NSLock`, not `Synchronization.Mutex`: the package floor is macOS 14). `AUHostRegistry` lost its private `RaceOutcome`/`raceAgainstTimeout`/`ResumeGate` (-51/+7) and both call sites now route through it. **DISCRIMINATION PROVED, NOT ARGUED** — a standalone harness (orchestrator re-ran it independently) built three variants under an identical 1 s main-actor hog with a 200 ms budget: OLD-A (shipped shape) **0/6**, **OLD-B (nonisolated arming + lock-free gate but deadline STILL `@MainActor`) 0/6** — the variant that isolates the single cause — and NEW **6/6** at 0.201–0.209 s. - ~~M4 (i) live mid-play send activation~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-06** (diagnostic round 3, per the parked method: stderr instrumentation + node-connection dump + preallocated-atomic tap probes + the live `diag-send.mjs` repro). Root cause was NOT the send wiring: the connection dump immediately after the rewire resume showed the mid-play-added leg fully attached and connected (source mixer → gain(vol 0.5) → bus sum → chain host → bus mixer, 48 kHz/2ch throughout) and the gain node's tap FIRING — carrying peak 0.0. Two stacked mechanisms produced the "silent until stop/play" symptom, on ALL strips (bus A metered 0.0000 after the resume too — the old E2E's poll windows just never caught it): (1) **THE BUG** — the resume anchored `derivedBeats` on `outputNode.lastRenderTime`, which right after the stop→reset→start bounce still reports the PREVIOUS render session's sample clock (valid flags set, measured sample=98304) while the restarted session's clock begins again near 0; the `max()` clamp then froze the playhead at the resume beat for the ENTIRE prior session length (unbounded in a long session — why it read as "silent forever"), postponing the loop-wrap revival past every poll (predicted wrap +4.19 s vs observed +4.17 s, 36 ms match). (2) The repro material (7.5-beat sustained MIDI chord) has no note-on between the resume beat and the wrap, and no-chase is the settled v0 contract (`MIDIEventSchedule`, ARCHITECTURE.md), so the resumed schedule was legitimately silent until the wrap — "stop/play revives it" was simply a restart from beat 0 with fresh note-ons, not a topology repair. FIX (one flag): the rewire resume calls `startPlayers(…, renderClockTrusted: false)`, forcing the already-proven host-clock anchor branch (host time is monotonic across the bounce; players start on hostTime anchors in both branches, so nothing else changes). Live post-fix: MIDI pad send meters on B at +2.29 s (= the wrap, level exactly matching the stop/play reference, no transport command, A uninterrupted-then-revived per the restart contract); audio-clip send meters at +0.26 s with A continuously intact; bus E2E 19/19 (fx-poll window widened to cover the no-chase wrap, with comment); suite 920/117 green; app stderr clean.
- ~~Teardown crash: `project.new` after a played send/bus project~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-12 (m13-a) — the crash class is dead BY CONSTRUCTION: once-rendered engines are never surgically detached; teardown-class changes discard and rebuild the whole engine.** Full arc, kept as the institutional record: **(1) 2026-07-06, discovery** during M4 (i) verification — build track→busA output + send→busB, `transport.play` ~1 s, `stop`, `project.new`, next `track.add` → SIGSEGV inside `-[AVAudioEngine connect:to:format:]` → `AVAudioEngineGraph::UpdateGraphAfterReconfig` → `swift_unknownObjectRelease` on a garbage pointer (`DAWApp-2026-07-06-051956.ips`; a sibling run crashed in a SwiftUI executor check, `…-051559.ips` — two surface stacks = heap corruption); the never-played variant did not crash. **(2) 2026-07-10, M9 crash-a fix** — diagnosis "detach against a stopped engine is unsafe"; mechanism = retire bin (`pendingDetachNodes` parked while stopped, `flushRetiredNodes()` after restart); live-verified 3× that day. **(3) 2026-07-12, FALSIFICATION** — the M13 audit (audit-m13.md B1) hit 3/3 staging sessions SIGSEGV'ing inside the fix's OWN flush path, and the m13-a C0 instrumented experiment named the mechanism with node-level evidence: after ONE engine stop→reset→start boundary, the FIRST flush-detach — of the routed source's strip mixer, with the engine RUNNING and `isRunning=true` logged at the call — is itself the faulting frame (instrumented addr `0x9ba885060 AVAudioMixerNode`, no survive line, `DAWApp-2026-07-12-104059.ips`; independently reproduced via `track.remove`, `…-104254.ips`). So "running at detach time" was NEVER sufficient: a node that RENDERED and then sat attached across a stop→reset→start boundary is already stale inside `AVAudioEngineGraph`'s internal node vector, and any later detach of it faults. The audit's "m12-f regression" suspicion was WRONG — same crash on the pre-m12-f binary; M9's 3× verification was heap-reuse luck. The C0 control leg (fresh-launch `project.new` ×20, engine never ran) survived 20/20, formally retiring the audit's session-3 "crash on first wire command" anomaly as mis-attribution (that shape cannot reach the crashing frame; plausible source = a foreign wire client, the documented 2026-07-11 staging-port anomaly). **(4) Resolution (m13-a; design docs/research/design-m13a-teardown-crash.md, supersedes fix-teardown-crash.md)** — retire-bin machinery deleted; announce-class reconcile on a once-rendered engine ABORTS before the first topology mutation and `AudioEngine.rebuildEngine(reason:)` discards the whole AVAudioEngine + PlaybackGraph and cold-builds from the model; `projectWillReplace()` forces the same rebuild unconditionally at project boundaries; `teardownDetach` detaches directly only against a running or never-run engine. Proven by the m13-a campaign: audit recipes verbatim + 12/12 played/unplayed × routed/plain matrix + 3× 41-track perf-c + 50-cycle soak (100 rebuilds, +0.4 MB RSS) + 20× fresh-launch — zero crashes, zero new .ips, m12-b offline anchors byte-identical, worst 41-track rebuild 143 ms.

- ~~Input device selection: pinned-device capture yields empty takes~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-05.** Root cause was NOT the eager pin wedging the AUHAL (disproved by CLI repro: eager prepare + pin still delivers tap buffers). Two stacked bugs: (1) the same-device guard compared the pin target against the AUHAL's `CurrentDevice`, which on a fresh AVAudioEngine is the engine's PRIVATE AGGREGATE device — never equal to any raw hardware ID — so every pinned take (default uid included) performed a real device set; (2) that set makes AVFoundation post `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` on the capture engine ~65 ms after start with the engine still running and the tap still healthy, and the config-change handler treated it as fatal → `stopRecording()` finalized the writer before the first buffer, and the writer's post-finalize guard silently swallowed every later delivery (hence zero frames AND zero stderr). Fix: pin skips when the uid resolves to the current system default (`InputDevices.defaultInputDeviceID()`); config-change handler only ends the take when the capture engine actually stopped; two-phase `InputCapture.prepare()/start(writer:)` replaces the eager pin; 1.5 s first-buffer watchdog aborts loudly ("no audio arrived from input device …") instead of a silent empty take. Live E2E green: default-uid pin, ZoomAudioDevice pin (frames flowed), unpinned.
